enum: Arkansas DHS’s current SNAP overview and time-limit pages identify the state’s operative ABAWD time-limit surface and state that the rules resumed July 1, 2023.

The four fixed Arkansas routes state that the requirement is waived in certain areas but do not recover a current FNS-approved ABAWD waiver instrument with complete covered geography and governing start and end dates.
Arkansas DHS identifies paystubs or an employer letter as possible work-hour evidence and assigns exemption and good-cause determinations to DHS after the recipient contacts the local county office.

California’s captured operative work-requirement and ABAWD authority is the CalFresh ABAWD Time Limit Handbook Version 3.0 issued through ACL 26-29, effective June 1, 2026, with ACL 26-43 as current supplemental administrative-data guidance.

California’s captured guidance permits self-attestation unless questionable, documentary evidence, collateral contacts, case-record and administrative-data evidence, and bounded county or eligibility-worker judgment with documentation duties.

Georgia DFCS’s current ABAWD page identifies the operative time-limit work-requirement surface, the December 1, 2023 through November 30, 2026 clock, and Georgia implementation for applications and recertifications submitted after November 1, 2025.

Georgia’s FFY 2026 plan anticipates zero ABAWDs in waived areas, but the fixed routes do not recover a current FNS-approved waiver instrument, covered geography, and complete governing period; a planning estimate is not an approval record.

Georgia’s FFY 2026 plan states that eligibility workers screen at application and renewal using the SNAP Policy manual and Oral Work Requirements script, request eligibility verification, document decisions in Georgia Gateway, and determine good cause from participant, employer, and other reliable information.

Maryland DHS’s current SNAP manual index identifies section 106 ABAWDS, revised September 2025 and posted October 16, 2025, and section 408 Verification, revised October 2025; the current ABAWD page states that the expanded requirements start November 1, 2025.

The fixed Maryland routes preserve a July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2026 three-month grace-period statement and an FFY 2026 planning estimate of zero ABAWDs in waived areas, but do not recover a current FNS-approved waiver instrument with complete geography and governing period.

Maryland’s current corpus identifies the October 2025 section 408 Verification manual, requires eligibility staff to complete Works Exemption screening, and provides for case-manager review of good cause, mental and physical fitness, and other work-requirement exemptions using participant, employer, provider, and system information.

North Carolina’s current NCDHHS work-requirement page states that revised ABAWD requirements took effect December 1, 2025, and the policy portal identifies FNS 260 ABAWD and FNS 265 ABAWD Services Program as the operative policy surfaces.

The four fixed North Carolina routes describe current ABAWD rules and exemption screening but do not recover a current FNS-approved waiver instrument with complete covered geography and governing start and end dates.

North Carolina states that county caseworkers screen at every application and recertification, provide at least ten days for requested verification, may accept an obvious condition without documentation, may seek statements from multiple professional sources when not obvious, and can assist when the client’s own statement is insufficient.

Pennsylvania DHS’s current federal-changes page and SNAP toolkit identify the operative work-and-reporting requirement surface, including staged September 1 and November 1, 2025 implementation materials and the current 80-hours-per-month reporting rule.

The fixed Pennsylvania routes describe current work and reporting requirements but do not recover a current FNS-approved ABAWD waiver instrument with complete covered geography and governing start and end dates; the two manual routes ended in transport failure.

Pennsylvania’s toolkit directs recipients to report work, education, training, or volunteer hours, states that caseworkers verify required hours every six months at renewal, and provides a COMPASS document-upload route; the corpus does not establish uniform worker execution.

Rhode Island DHS’s current SNAP updates page states that the revised ABAWD requirements begin March 1, 2026 and preserves current exemption and activity-reporting forms revised through March 23, 2026; the FFY 2026 plan supplies the approved state E&T authority surface.

The fixed Rhode Island routes describe current ABAWD requirements and exemption forms but do not recover a current FNS-approved waiver instrument with complete covered geography and governing start and end dates.

Rhode Island preserves community-partner and client exemption-request forms, an activity-reporting form, a SNAP verification checklist, and FFY 2026 plan procedures under which staff apply screening criteria, require verification for specified criteria, document contacts in the case file, and process provider determinations.
The current South Dakota manual is marked Updated July 2026, but the fixed corpus does not recover an exact effective date for the complete current implementation authority.
South Dakota’s FY2025 waiver is preserved as an expired predecessor, while the fixed corpus does not recover a complete current waiver approval and governing period.

Washington’s captured operative ABAWD authority is the permanent adoption WSR 26-10-028 for WAC 388-444-0030 and 388-444-0035, effective July 1, 2026, together with the current EA-Z ABAWD chapter and revision custody.

Washington’s captured current pages say all areas became subject to the time limit and no areas were waived as of February 1, 2026, but the complete current governing period or successor end state is not publicly recovered.

West Virginia’s approved FFY 2026 plan identifies the Division of Family Assistance as the policy authority and states that SNAP E&T policy is in Chapter 17 of the Income Maintenance Manual, with the broader policy resource in Chapters 3 and 17.

West Virginia’s FFY 2026 plan anticipates zero ABAWDs in waived areas, but the fixed routes do not recover a current FNS-approved waiver instrument, covered geography, and complete governing period; two state notices returned 404 and the portal capture was content-insufficient.

West Virginia’s FFY 2026 plan states that eligibility workers evaluate reported good cause from participant, employer, provider, and case information, may exercise discretion for circumstances outside the participant’s control, issue a ten-day verification request, document provider determinations, and use system verification links and data matching.
Montana's captured public SNAP authority consists of the SNAP 0-1 manual index issued or revised July 1, 2026 together with SNAP 700 Work Registration effective June 1, 2025.
Montana's captured work-registration section is effective June 1, 2025, and its captured geographic-waiver section is effective November 1, 2025.
Montana SNAP 802-1 states that, as of November 1, 2025, no areas within Montana have approved ABAWD geographic waivers.

North Dakota's official SNAP Release Log identifies the current public release boundary as Release 26.5, effective June 15, 2026, and records section 301 Work Registration changes in Releases 26.1, 26.4, and 26.5.
North Dakota policy section 403 Geographic Waiver states an effective date of November 1, 2025 and identifies Release 25.7.

North Dakota's exact FY2025 partial approval expired June 30, 2026; three page-complete FY2026 federal snapshots classify North Dakota as partial on October 1, 2025, January 1, 2026, and March 1, 2026 without identifying the active geography or one implementation-to-expiration interval; the current state section does not resolve that mismatch; the complete correct-range MI-NM request-support archive contains no North Dakota-scoped member; and the final authorized current-index refresh is byte-identical to the July 22 baseline with no North Dakota FY2026 response anchor.
